lead: A full-moon name is a starting point, not a complete identification. For a seasonal food guide, the month, locality and particular observance matter: an offering at Kumar Purnima cannot simply become the menu for Pandu Purnima.

sections.title: Two inventory names still need an identity
sections.text: Pratap Kumar Dash’s 2006 list names Benatia Osha and Purnima Osha without separate descriptions. The original page does not supply their stories, months or foods. A parenthesis mentioning Kartika and Shiva follows Bada Osha; it is not used here to fill the preceding entries. Benatia’s Odia spelling, locality and possible aliases remain unverified.

sections.title: Why the full-moon label is not enough
sections.text: Mahanti separately names Aswina’s Kumara Purnima and Margasira’s Pandu Purnima. The saved collection also covers the Kartika/Rai Damodara vow. These give readers distinct routes into seasonal practice, but do not identify which observance Dash intended by the unqualified Purnima Osha entry.
sections.locator: Printed24,26 / PDF40,42; existing Rai Damodara profile

sections.title: Stories and histories stay with their named observance
sections.text: Follow the linked profiles for their attributed narratives and dating limits. Shared moon worship, a similar offering shape or a repeated word does not establish a common origin. This guide does not create a combined Purnima story or assign a history to Benatia.

sections.title: What to ask before looking for seasonal food
sections.text: Record the local name and month first, then distinguish an offering from a fast-breaking meal, a game material or ritual drawing paste. A participant’s account should retain its locality and permission to share. Current annual dates, public access, host consent and serving venues need separate evidence; none is established by this guide.
